directAnswer: Pope Innocent VIII was Giovanni Battista Cibo of Genoa, who reigned from 1484 to 1492. His pontificate is remembered for the bull Summis desiderantes affectibus on witchcraft, a costly war with Naples, the custody of the Ottoman prince Cem in Rome, and close ties to the Medici of Florence.

paras: Giovanni Battista Cibo was born in Genoa in 1432 to a family of Roman senatorial standing. Before his ordination he fathered children, whom he later acknowledged openly as pope, including his son Franceschetto. He entered papal service, became bishop of Savona and later Molfetta, and was created a cardinal by Sixtus IV in 1473.

In the conclave of August 1484, Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere played a decisive role in securing Cibo's election. Innocent VIII was regarded as amiable but easily guided, and della Rovere remained one of the most influential men at his court.

sections.h2: Summis Desiderantes and the Witch Trials
paras: In December 1484 Innocent VIII issued the bull Summis desiderantes affectibus at the request of the Dominican inquisitor Heinrich Kramer, granting him and a colleague authority to pursue alleged witchcraft in parts of Germany. Kramer later printed the bull at the front of his notorious handbook, the Malleus Maleficarum, lending it an air of papal approval it did not formally have.

In Spain, Innocent VIII in 1487 confirmed Tomas de Torquemada as grand inquisitor of the Spanish tribunal established under Sixtus IV. He also had a commission examine the 900 theses of Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, several of which were condemned in 1487.

sections.h2: War with Naples and the Medici Alliance
paras: Early in his reign the pope was drawn into the so-called Barons' War, backing rebellious nobles against King Ferrante of Naples. The conflict drained the papal treasury and ended in 1486 without lasting gains.

Innocent VIII then drew close to Lorenzo de' Medici. His son Franceschetto married Lorenzo's daughter Maddalena, and in 1489 the pope named Lorenzo's thirteen-year-old son Giovanni a cardinal, on condition that the appointment remain secret for three years. That boy would become Pope Leo X.

sections.h2: Prince Cem and the Holy Lance
paras: From 1489 Rome held as an honored captive Prince Cem, brother and rival of the Ottoman sultan Bayezid II. In return for keeping him from leading a revolt, the sultan paid the papacy an annual sum and in 1492 sent the relic venerated as the Holy Lance, which is still kept at St. Peter's.

Innocent VIII also built the Belvedere villa on the Vatican hill. He died on 25 July 1492, months after the fall of Granada ended Muslim rule in Spain and only days before Columbus sailed. Lurid stories about his final days circulated later but are not supported by reliable sources.

keyFacts: Born Giovanni Battista Cibo in Genoa in 1432
Issued the bull Summis desiderantes affectibus on witchcraft (1484)
Confirmed Tomas de Torquemada as Spanish grand inquisitor (1487)
Made Giovanni de' Medici, the future Leo X, a cardinal at 13
Received the relic of the Holy Lance from Sultan Bayezid II (1492)

faqs.question: Did Innocent VIII approve the Malleus Maleficarum?
faqs.answer: No. He issued Summis desiderantes affectibus in 1484 empowering inquisitors in Germany, and the author of the Malleus later printed that bull in his book. The pope never formally endorsed the handbook itself.

faqs.question: Who was Prince Cem and why was he in Rome?
faqs.answer: Cem was a brother and rival of Sultan Bayezid II. Held in papal custody from 1489, he was a political asset; the sultan paid for his detention and sent the relic of the Holy Lance to Rome.

faqs.question: How was Innocent VIII connected to the Medici?
faqs.answer: His son married Lorenzo de' Medici's daughter, and he named Lorenzo's son Giovanni a cardinal at age 13. Giovanni later became Pope Leo X.
